metadata.title: The Diner Break-In
metadata.description: A small-time overnight burglary at a 24-hour diner leaves a broken back door and the cash drawer emptied, with no injuries reported.
metadata.briefing: Someone forced the back door of a 24-hour diner before dawn and made off with cash. The scene looks simple, but the short window and familiar routines narrow the field fast.

assets.title: Back Door Damage (Exterior)
assets.description: Exterior close-up of the diner's rear service door showing fresh pry damage and splintering around the latch. The photo highlights distinct tool-mark striations and paint transfer on the metal strike plate for later comparison.

assets.title: Register & Empty Cash Drawer
assets.description: Crime-scene photo of the front POS counter showing the register with its cash drawer pulled open and emptied. Captures the disturbed state of the workstation, what was left behind, and the surrounding counter area for context.

assets.title: Diner Layout & Back-Alley Access Sketch
assets.description: Hand-drawn layout sketch of the diner interior and rear alley access, prepared during the initial scene walkthrough. Notes door swing, camera sightlines, and the shortest path from the back door to the front POS/register area.

assets.title: Cash-Drop/Closing Procedure Sheet
assets.description: Printed cash-handling and closing instructions posted in the office, outlining when cash should be removed from the register and who is responsible. The sheet highlights predictable windows when cash could remain in the drawer and indicates managerial access and knowledge of the routine.

assets.title: POS Transaction Log (02:45–03:45)
assets.description: Exported POS transaction and event log covering the hour around the 03:18 break-in. It time-stamps register activity at the front counter to corroborate staff location and actions during the incident window.

assets.title: Dining Area CCTV Clip (03:00–03:30)
assets.description: Interior dining-area CCTV covering the front counter and main floor during the break-in window. Shows staff/customer positions and activity consistent with the POS timestamps, helping rule out who could have accessed the back door unnoticed.

assets.title: Across-the-Street Alley Camera Still
assets.description: A single still frame from an exterior security camera across the street, capturing the diner’s back-alley approach during the 03:18 a.m. break-in window. It shows who was present near the rear entrance and whether anyone moved toward the back door at that time.

assets.title: Kitchen/Back Door Chime Entry Log
assets.description: A timestamped export from the kitchen/back-door chime sensor showing door-open events during the break-in window. Used to corroborate staff movements and whether the back door was opened around 03:18.

assets.title: Toolmark Comparison Report: Rear Door Pry Damage
assets.description: Microscopic toolmark comparison of the rear service door’s pry damage documents striation and paint-transfer features consistent with a pry tool associated with Raymond Holtman. The report summarizes chain of custody, comparative methodology, and the basis for the association.

emails.subject: Immediate Assignment: The Diner Break-In — Eugene (05/11, 0318 hrs)
emails.body:
Detective Morgan,

You’re assigned the overnight burglary at the 24-hour diner in Eugene, Oregon, reported from an incident window centered at approximately 0318 hours on 05/11. The victim is the business itself—no injuries—but the back door shows forced-entry damage and the register cash drawer was emptied. Treat this as an active, time-sensitive investigation while memories and video retention windows are still intact.

Respond to the location as soon as practicable, coordinate with patrol for scene preservation, and ensure the back-door tool marks and latch/strike damage are properly documented. Collect and secure the initial assets already flagged: exterior back door damage photo, register/cash drawer photo, the back-alley access sketch, and the cash-drop/closing procedure sheet.

Move quickly on digital corroboration. Pull the POS transaction export (0245–0345), dining area CCTV clip (0300–0330), the across-the-street alley camera still, and the kitchen/back door chime entry log. Establish a precise entry/exit timeline and identify any gaps in coverage or discrepancies between logs, video, and statements.

Interview the overnight staff and any late-night customers immediately, but do it quietly. Stress to all parties that this is an internal administrative matter until we complete baseline fact-checking; we do not want rumors or finger-pointing circulating through the diner, ownership, or local media.

Use discretion in all communications—no speculation, no names discussed outside the investigative chain, and keep your notes and requests tightly controlled. I want an initial findings update by end of shift today, with any urgent leads elevated as they surface.

—Chief Marisol Herrera

emails.subject: Re: Incident 05/11 — what I saw on overnight shift
emails.body:
Detective,

I’m the overnight server. At about 3:15–3:20 a.m. I was up front between the counter and tables because two customers were still in the dining area. I remember running a card payment at the front POS around then.

I did not go near the back door during that time. I didn’t hear the back door chime right away over the kitchen noise, but I noticed a weird draft a few minutes later and the kitchen door seemed to swing more than normal.

I will say the cash-drop routine has been inconsistent lately. Some nights the drawer sits with more cash than it should until the next drop. Raymond is usually the one who talks about the procedure and has the keys/lock stuff.

—Zoe

emails.subject: My smoke break timing / back door
emails.body:
Whoever’s working this,

I was on my smoke break out back around 3:10ish. I stayed behind the building by the alley like I always do. I came back in a little after 3:20.

The back door has been sticky for weeks. Sometimes you have to pull it hard to get it shut and it doesn’t always latch clean unless you push it. I’ve told Raymond that more than once and he said he’d “take care of it.”

I didn’t pry anything and I didn’t go to the register.

—Miles

emails.subject: Diner Break-In — initial context & priorities
emails.body:
Detective,

Initial walk-through indicates forced entry at the rear service door and a quick path taken to the front POS/cash drawer. No injuries; minimal disturbance beyond the door and register area.

Priorities today:
1) Lock down who had operational knowledge of cash-drop timing and access to keys/door maintenance.
2) Reconcile staff movements against POS/CCTV/chime data.
3) Canvass for anyone familiar with the alley approach.

Keep interviews tight and contemporaneous; this is likely someone who understood the routine.

—Chief Herrera

emails.subject: Toolmark Comparison Completed — Rear Door Pry Damage (Case case_rookie_demo)
emails.body:
Toolmark comparison of the submitted image **asset.back_door_damage_photo** (rear service door pry damage) has been completed for case **case_rookie_demo** (incident **2026-05-11 03:18 PT**; case opened **2026-05-11 08:42 PT**).

The strike-plate abrasion and adjacent pry impression display class characteristics consistent with prying by a flat-edged implement. In the clearest regions of the image, the mark contains a repeatable, parallel striation set with a stable orientation and spacing, along the same path as localized paint transfer.

Those striation and paint-transfer features are consistent with reference characteristics documented for a pry tool associated with **Raymond Holtman**. Within the limitations of photo-based comparison, the correspondences support a common source (i.e., the Holtman-linked tool) over an unrelated tool of similar class.

Please note the limitation that the substrate/tool were not physically examined; if the tool and door hardware can be submitted, controlled test-mark comparisons would strengthen the conclusion. The full PDF report has been added to the case file as **Toolmark Comparison Report: Rear Door Pry Damage**.

suspects.name: Zoe Caldwell
suspects.relationship: Employee who closed the register before the break-in
suspects.motive: She was under pressure about short tips and a recent warning over minor till discrepancies, giving her a reason to want quick cash. She also knew the closing routine and where the drawer would be easiest to access if procedures were sloppy.
suspects.alibi: At the time of the break-in she was on the floor serving two late-night customers and ringing a card payment at the front POS, then clocked out shortly after. The POS timestamps and the customers’ statements place her inside the dining area during the window of entry.
suspects.background: Zoe is a newer hire on the overnight shift, known for following checklists and being meticulous about end-of-shift side work. She’s had minor friction with management over being blamed for register issues she says come from inconsistent cash-drop procedures. Coworkers describe her as tired but steady, more anxious about keeping the job than looking for trouble.

suspects.name: Miles Kruger
suspects.relationship: Coworker at the diner; works nights with the overnight staff
suspects.motive: He’s been complaining about reduced hours and tips and is known to be short on cash, which makes the emptied drawer look tempting. His frequent smoke breaks by the back door also put him close to the point of entry.
suspects.alibi: At the time of the break-in, he was on a scheduled smoke break behind the building, then came back in and resumed prep. The alley-facing security camera across the street captures him outside during the window, and his re-entry is timestamped on the kitchen door chime log.
suspects.background: Miles is a steady but prickly late-shift line cook who prefers the quiet hours and keeps to himself between rushes. He’s a habitual smoker and often uses the back door, which has made other staff suspicious when anything goes missing. Despite the grumbling about pay, he’s generally reliable in the kitchen and avoids confrontation with management.

suspects.name: Raymond Holtman
suspects.relationship: Victim business’s day manager with access to keys and cash procedures
suspects.motive: Raymond was under pressure from overdue bills and a recent warning from ownership about cash discrepancies. Staging a back-door break-in let him cover the theft as an outside job while exploiting his knowledge of the cash-drop routine.
suspects.alibi: He claims he was home asleep and briefly on a late-night call with his sister around 3:10 a.m., then never left his apartment. Phone records show a call occurred, but it doesn’t prove he stayed home and the duration is shorter than he stated.
suspects.background: Raymond has managed the diner’s daytime operations for years and is trusted with keys, lock maintenance, and register reconciliation. Coworkers describe him as strict about procedures but increasingly irritable in the weeks leading up to the break-in. He knows the back door’s weak points and when cash is most likely to be in the drawer between drops.

suspects.name: Tessa Morrow
suspects.relationship: Regular late-night customer at the diner
suspects.motive: She resents being informally cut off from lingering at the counter and has complained about staff “treating her like a problem.” She also knows the diner’s late-night routines well enough that the cash drawer theft would look tempting on paper.
suspects.alibi: At the time of the break-in, she was on a recorded customer-support call at her employer’s office, ending minutes after 3:18 a.m. Badge-entry logs and the call recording place her inside the call center during the incident window.
suspects.background:
Tessa is a habitual after-midnight diner regular who talks to staff and watches the rhythm of closing tasks, cash handling, and back-of-house traffic.
Her presence has made employees uneasy, more because of persistence than aggression, and she’s been asked more than once not to loiter after buying coffee.
She keeps irregular hours due to night work and tends to document small grievances, which makes her sound calculating even when she isn’t.

suspects.name: Caleb Stroud
suspects.relationship: Occasional late-night delivery driver who uses the diner's back alley turnaround
suspects.motive: He knows the alley and the back door area well from nightly turnarounds, and quick cash could tempt someone with irregular pay. Being seen near the rear entrance around odd hours makes him an easy person to suspect.
suspects.alibi: At the time of the break-in, he was on an active delivery route and was recorded at a gas station checkout a few minutes away, then continued to his next drop. Route logs and time-stamped receipts place him away from the diner during the window.
suspects.background: Caleb runs late-night deliveries for a local convenience distributor and often uses the diner's back alley to avoid tight turns on the main street. Staff recognize his van and have occasionally waved him through when the alley is busy. He keeps to himself and is more familiar with the alley layout than the diner interior, which makes him noticeable but not necessarily involved.

timeline.event: Raymond Holtman reports being on a late-night phone call with his sister around this time; phone records confirm a call occurred but not his location or claimed duration.
Across-the-street alley camera captures Miles Kruger outside behind the diner during his scheduled smoke break, placing him near the back door shortly before the break-in window.
Back door is forced and the cash drawer is emptied; no injuries are reported.
Kitchen/back door chime entry log records back-area door activity consistent with someone entering/exiting through the rear during the incident window.
Dining area CCTV and the POS transaction export place Zoe Caldwell at the front register and on the floor serving customers during the break-in window.
Miles Kruger is timestamped returning from outside; the alley camera and the kitchen door chime log support his re-entry timing.
Scene is documented: exterior back-door damage and tool-mark patterns are photographed; register and empty cash drawer are photographed for condition and disturbance.
Case is formally opened by the chief; initial evidence package includes CCTV clip, POS export, alley camera still, back-door chime log, and cash procedure sheet.

forensicOutcomes.conclusionText: Microscopic comparison of the photographed pry damage indicates a consistent striation pattern and paint-transfer characteristics with a pry tool associated with Raymond Holtman. The observed correspondences support that the same tool type—and likely the same tool—was used to force the diner’s rear door during the 2026-05-11 incident window.

Digital timeline reconstruction of the POS transaction/event export (02:45–03:45 on 2026-05-11) corroborates activity at the front register during the incident window, including staff presence consistent with other records. The POS data does not provide attribution for the rear-door entry or identify the person who accessed the back area at approximately 03:18.

Digital timeline reconstruction of the dining-area CCTV clip (03:00–03:30) corroborates staff and customer positions at the front counter during the 03:18 incident window and is consistent with the corresponding front-of-house activity. The video does not capture the rear entry point or any identifiable view of the person accessing the back door, and no unique identifying features of the intruder can be derived from this asset.

Examination of the Cash-Drop/Closing Procedure Sheet found no indications of alteration, added markings, or distinctive authorship features that would attribute the document to a specific individual. The document is consistent with a routine posted instruction sheet and provides only general contextual information about cash-handling timing and access.

questions.prompt: Which investigative method most directly linked the break-in to Raymond Holtman?

options.label: Microscopic toolmark comparison of rear-door pry damage to a pry tool tied to Raymond
Digital reconstruction correlating POS logs and dining-area CCTV timestamps
Document examination of the cash-drop/closing procedure sheet for alterations
Phone-record verification of Raymond’s late-night call duration and timing

questions.prompt: Where did the diner break-in take place?
Which event occurs immediately after the 03:18 break-in in the timeline?

options.label: 03:19 kitchen/back door chime records rear-area door activity
03:20 POS/CCTV place Zoe at the front register serving customers
03:22 Miles is timestamped returning from outside
03:25 scene photos document door damage and the empty cash drawer

questions.prompt: What most likely motivated the staged back-door break-in at the diner?

options.label: Cover personal theft by making it look like an outside burglary, amid overdue bills and cash-discrepancy pressure
Retaliate against ownership for stricter cash procedures and recent reprimands
Take advantage of a predictable cash-drop window for quick, low-risk cash
Create suspicion around overnight staff by exploiting their access routines

solution.explanation:
Raymond Holtman staged the “break-in” to cover a cash theft: the **Toolmark Comparison Report** ties the rear door pry striations and paint transfer to a pry tool associated with him, and the **kitchen/back-door chime log** shows rear-door activity right at the 03:18 window when the drawer was emptied. The **alley camera still** supports the timeline by showing who was actually in the back-alley approach during the incident window, while Raymond’s phone-call alibi is unverified and doesn’t fix his location.

**Zoe Caldwell** is cleared by POS timestamps and dining-area CCTV placing her at the front register with customers; **Miles Kruger** is cleared by the alley camera and his logged re-entry timing matching his smoke break; **Tessa Morrow** is cleared by badge-entry and a recorded call at her workplace; **Caleb Stroud** is cleared by delivery-route logs and time-stamped receipts placing him away from the diner.
